sections.content: If you've been searching for real estate deals in Paterson NJ, you're not alone — and you're onto something. Just 15 miles west of Midtown Manhattan, Paterson is one of New Jersey's largest cities and one of its most undervalued real estate markets. While neighboring areas like Montclair and Hackensack have seen prices climb out of range for many investors, Paterson still offers entry points where the numbers can actually work. Whether you're a seasoned wholesaler, a first-time flipper, or a buy-and-hold landlord, this market deserves a serious look. If you're newer to the game, start with our Real Estate Investing for Beginners guide to build your foundation before diving into a market like Paterson.
Paterson NJ Market Overview: What Investors Need to Know

Paterson is a city of about 160,000 people in Passaic County, New Jersey. It has a rich industrial history — it was once called the 'Silk City' for its textile manufacturing — and today it's a dense, working-class urban market with strong rental demand. The city has a high percentage of renters, with roughly 70% of households renting rather than owning. That single statistic tells you a lot about the opportunity here for landlords and buy-and-hold investors.

The median home price in Paterson hovers around $350,000 to $390,000 as of 2024, depending on property type and neighborhood. That's significantly lower than the broader Bergen and Essex County markets, where comparable homes can easily exceed $550,000 to $700,000. Multi-family properties — two, three, and four-unit buildings — are where many investors focus their attention, and those typically range from $400,000 to $600,000 depending on condition and location. For wholesalers, motivated seller leads exist throughout the city, with distressed properties regularly trading at $200,000 to $280,000 before renovations.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investment in Paterson NJ

Not all of Paterson is created equal. Like any urban market, the city has pockets of strong investment potential and areas that require more caution. Knowing where to focus your energy is half the battle.
Eastside

The Eastside neighborhood is generally considered one of the more stable and desirable areas in Paterson. Property values here tend to be slightly higher, but so is tenant quality and rental demand. Investors targeting buy-and-hold or BRRRR strategies often prioritize Eastside because vacancy rates are lower and properties hold their value better over time.
Bunker Hill and Hillcrest

These neighborhoods sit on elevated ground in the western and northern parts of the city. Bunker Hill in particular has seen increased interest from investors over the past three to four years as buyers have been priced out of nearby towns. Multi-family properties here often generate gross rents of $3,500 to $5,000 per month on two- and three-unit buildings, which can produce solid cash flow when purchased at the right price.
Downtown and Great Falls Area

The Great Falls National Historical Park has brought renewed attention to downtown Paterson. There's been gradual revitalization near the waterfront, and the city has received state and federal funding for economic development in this corridor. For investors with a longer time horizon, this area represents speculative upside — higher risk, but potentially higher reward as gentrification pressure from neighboring markets continues to push eastward.

Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Paterson NJ
Wholesale Deals

Paterson has an active wholesale market. The city has a significant number of aging homeowners, absentee landlords with tired portfolios, and estate sales — all prime sources for motivated sellers. Wholesalers typically target properties needing $40,000 to $100,000 in repairs and aim to put them under contract at 60 to 65 cents on the dollar of ARV. If ARV on a Paterson single-family is $380,000 and repairs run $70,000, a wholesaler might target a contract price of $145,000 to $160,000. Learning how to find off-market real estate deals is essential in a market like Paterson, where the best opportunities rarely hit the MLS.
Fix and Flip

Fix-and-flip investors have found Paterson to be a workable market, though margins are tighter than in some suburban New Jersey markets. A successful flip here typically targets a buy price of 65 to 70% of ARV minus repairs. On a property with a $400,000 ARV and $80,000 in renovations, you'd aim to acquire for no more than $180,000 to $200,000. Flippers who know how to work with local contractors and understand buyer preferences in the market can net $40,000 to $70,000 per deal. Understanding how to analyze real estate deals is critical before you commit capital to any flip project.
Buy-and-Hold Rentals

This is arguably the strongest strategy in Paterson given the city's overwhelming renter population. A well-purchased three-unit property can generate $5,500 to $7,500 in monthly gross rent. If purchased at $420,000 with 25% down and a 7% interest rate, monthly PITI runs approximately $2,800 to $3,000, leaving room for a cash-on-cash return of 6 to 10% depending on expenses and vacancy. The BRRRR method — Buy, Rehab, Rent, Refinance, Repeat — is particularly popular among Paterson investors because distressed multi-families can often be acquired well below market value. sections.content: Paterson NJ Real Estate Market Trends in 2024

Paterson's market has shown resilience even as rising interest rates cooled many suburban New Jersey markets in 2023 and 2024. Because Paterson's price points are lower and rental demand is structurally strong, the market absorbed rate increases better than higher-priced surrounding areas. Days on market increased from an average of 18 days in 2022 to roughly 35 to 45 days in 2024 for retail listings, which has actually created better buying opportunities for investors who negotiate off-market. Home values have appreciated approximately 8 to 12% since 2020, and while appreciation has slowed, fundamentals remain solid. Immigration continues to drive population stability in Paterson, which directly supports rental demand — a key factor for landlords.

Paterson fits that description precisely.' — Common wisdom among New Jersey real estate investors
Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting Paterson NJ

Paterson attracts interest from investors across the country, particularly from the South and Midwest where buyers appreciate New Jersey's strong rental yields relative to acquisition costs. But investing from out of state comes with real risks if you don't build the right local infrastructure.

items: Build a local team first: Find a boots-on-the-ground real estate agent, a licensed NJ property manager, and a local contractor before making an offer. New Jersey has strict landlord-tenant laws that favor tenants — you need local expertise.

Understand NJ landlord-tenant law: New Jersey is a tenant-friendly state. Evictions can take 3 to 9 months. Always run thorough tenant screening and work with a local attorney familiar with Passaic County courts.

Visit before you buy: Even one site visit to walk properties and meet your local team dramatically reduces risk. Use that trip to tour multiple neighborhoods and get a feel for block-by-block conditions.

Use technology to source deals: Platforms like AIWholesail let out-of-state investors find and analyze deals in target markets like Paterson without being on the ground full-time. Explore the Paterson NJ market hub to see current deal activity.

Run the numbers conservatively: Account for 10% vacancy, 10% property management, and a 10 to 15% repairs and maintenance reserve. Paterson's older housing stock means maintenance costs can be higher than expected.

Focus on multi-family: Single-family rentals in Paterson can be cash flow neutral or negative after expenses. Two- to four-unit properties provide the income diversification that makes the numbers work even with one vacant unit.

Is Paterson NJ Right for Your Investment Strategy?

Paterson NJ is not a market for passive investors who want turnkey properties and zero headaches. It's an urban market that rewards investors who are willing to do their homework, build strong local teams, and be patient with the process. The upside is real: strong rental demand, prices still accessible compared to the broader NY metro area, and a consistent flow of distressed inventory for wholesalers and flippers. If you're willing to treat this like a business rather than a side project, Paterson can deliver consistent returns that are increasingly hard to find in the Northeast.
